questions.q: In a browser, **Ctrl+9** jumps to —
questions.solution: Ctrl+1–8 pick tab numbers 1–8, but **Ctrl+9 always goes to the rightmost (last) tab**, however many are open.

questions.q: Which pair is wrongly matched?
questions.solution: Wi-Fi is **802.11**; 802.3 is the wired Ethernet standard — the planted swap.

questions.q: In MS Excel, pressing Ctrl+Space selects:
questions.solution: Ctrl+Space selects the whole column of the active cell and Shift+Space selects the whole row. Ctrl+A selects the data region, or the whole sheet if pressed again.
questions.shortcut: Ctrl and Column both start with C; Shift+Space = row.

questions.q: In the URL https://www.gov.in/schemes/2026.html, the part '/schemes/2026.html' is the —
options: Path to the page on the server
questions.solution: https = protocol, www.gov.in = domain, and everything after is the **path** to the exact file.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (4).
questions.solution: The nurses state their reason for borrowing: '___ the magazines remind them of the hospital's own reading room.' The second clause answers *why* they keep borrowing → **because**. *Until* and *unless* change the logic to time and condition, and *although* would need the borrowing to be surprising — it is not.
questions.shortcut: If the clause after the blank answers 'why?', choose because/since.
questions.passage: The tea stall outside the district hospital has become an unlikely reading point. The owner, Joseph, keeps a shelf of old magazines beside the stove, and customers read them (1) ______ their tea cools. His regulars first laughed at the shelf, (2) ______ today even senior nurses borrow his weeklies. Business has not suffered at all; (3) ______, some customers now order a second cup to finish an article. Nurses say they keep borrowing (4) ______ the magazines remind them of the hospital's own reading room.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: **Deficiency** follows deficient: the c sounds 'sh' (de-FI-shen-see), so the letters are **-ciency**, like efficiency and proficiency. The f is single.
questions.shortcut: Every -ciency word keeps ie after c.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: The statement uses **have** with the subject *the students* → the tag flips it: **haven't they?** 'Isn't it?' matches neither the helper nor the subject.
questions.shortcut: tag = helping verb flipped + subject pronoun.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: Needed meaning: misplace → **lose**. *Loose* means 'not tight' and *loosen* means 'make less tight' — neither fits.

questions.q: **Adrenaline**, the 'fight-or-flight' hormone, is secreted by the —
questions.solution: **Adrenal glands** (on the kidneys) release adrenaline in emergencies — faster heartbeat, more blood sugar, instant energy.

questions.q: The **television** was invented by —
questions.solution: The Scottish inventor **John Logie Baird** demonstrated television in 1926. Marconi is radio; Faraday worked on electromagnetic induction.

questions.q: Gandhi's **first satyagraha in India** was launched at —
questions.solution: **Champaran (Bihar), 1917**, against the tinkathia indigo system — Rajkumar Shukla had persuaded Gandhi to come.

questions.q:
Who among the following were the members of the **Cabinet Mission (1946)**?
1. Lord Pethick-Lawrence
2. Stafford Cripps
3. A.V. Alexander
4. Lord Wavell
questions.solution: The **Cabinet Mission** = Pethick-Lawrence (Secretary of State), **Cripps** and **Alexander**. Wavell was the Viceroy, not a mission member.

questions.q: An article costing ₹1,000 is marked 25% above cost and then sold at a 15% discount. The profit earned is:
The compound interest on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years is:
The average of 5 numbers is 27. Four of the numbers are 23, 25, 28 and 26. The fifth number is:
questions.solution: Total $=5\times27=135$; given sum $=102$; fifth $=135-102=33$.

questions.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are in the ratio $5:12$ and its area is $120$ sq cm. The perimeter of the rhombus is:
questions.solution:
$d_1 = 5k$, $d_2 = 12k$: $\frac12 \times 60k^2 = 120 \Rightarrow k^2 = 4 \Rightarrow k = 2$.

Diagonals 10 and 24 → side 13 → perimeter $52$ cm.
questions.shortcut: $30k^2 = 120$ → $k = 2$; 5-12-13 halves → $52$ cm. Trap: $48$ (side 12 from one diagonal).

questions.q:
Find the missing number:

**3   12**

**7   28**

**9   ?**
questions.solution: Second number = 4 × first: 3 × 4 = 12 ✓, 7 × 4 = 28 ✓. So 9 × 4 = **36**. (27 uses ×3, which fits neither row.)
questions.shortcut: Divide the output by the input — a constant quotient means a constant multiplier.

questions.q: All arrangements of the letters of **BEAD** are listed as in a dictionary. What is the **position of BEAD** in that list?
questions.solution: Sorted letters: A, B, D, E. B → 1 smaller (A) × 3! = 6. E → unused {A, D, E}: 2 smaller × 2! = 4. A → 0. D → 0. Rank = 6 + 4 + 0 + 0 + 1 = **11**.

questions.solution: The correct figure sits in the **upper-left part** of the given figure, with every line matching in direction and length. The other three options are the same shape shown as its mirror (left-right flip), a copy turned through 90 degrees and a copy turned through 180 degrees — none of them can be traced in the figure without turning it, and rotation is not allowed.
questions.shortcut: Fix the most distinctive stroke (a lone diagonal or an odd-length line), locate it in the main figure, then check the rest.

questions.q: Which set of signs will make **12 ? 4 ? 2 = 6** correct?
questions.shortcut: The ÷/× pair works rank-to-rank left to right: 12 ÷ 4 × 2 — divide first, then multiply.
